# Student Attendance Record I.

@example The late days come in two pairs split by a P, and there is one absence.
"LLPLLAP"
=> true

@example Two absences break the first rule, even though they are far apart.
"PAPPPA"
=> false

@example Three late days in a row break the second rule.
"PLLLP"
=> false

# A single day, of each kind.
"A"
=> true

"L"
=> true

"P"
=> true

# Two absences in a row.
"AA"
=> false

# Two late days in a row are fine; three are not.
"LL"
=> true

"LLL"
=> false

# Three late days at the start, and at the end, where no later day ends
# the run.
"LLLPA"
=> false

"LPLLL"
=> false

# An A between late days breaks the run too; a second A breaks the first
# rule.
"LLALL"
=> true

"LLALLA"
=> false

# Both rules broken.
"ALLLA"
=> false

# Absent on the first and the last day.
"APPPPPPPA"
=> false

# Many late days, never three in a row, and one absence; then four late
# days in a row.
"LLPLLPLPLLALLPL"
=> true

"PLLLLP"
=> false

# 128, 256 and 257 absences: an 8-bit counter goes negative or wraps to
# 0 or 1.
"APAPAPAPAPAPAPAPAPAPAPAPAPAPAPAPAPAPAPAPAPAPAPAPAPAPAPAPAPAPAPAPAPAPAPAPAPAPAPAPAPAPAPAPAPAPAPAPAPAPAPAPAPAPAPAPAPAPAPAPAPAPAPAPAPAPAPAPAPAPAPAPAPAPAPAPAPAPAPAPAPAPAPAPAPAPAPAPAPAPAPAPAPAPAPAPAPAPAPAPAPAPAPAPAPAPAPAPAPAPAPAPAPAPAPAPAPAPAPAPAPAPAPAPAPAPAPAP"
=> false

"AAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAA"
=> false

"PAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAA"
=> false

# Late runs of 256, 257 and 258 days, no absence before the last day.
"LLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLL"
=> false

"PLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLP"
=> false

"LLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLA"
=> false

# The longest logs: all present, all late, and late pairs with a single
# absence on the last day.
""
=> true

""
=> false

""
=> true

# Random small cases from gen.c (lc check --regen makes them).
@gen 1 small
"PPP"
=> true

@gen 2 small
"PPPLL"
=> true

@gen 3 small
"PPPPPPPPLPPP"
=> true

@gen 4 small
"LPLLPPPL"
=> true

@gen 5 small
"LLLPPLLLLL"
=> false

@gen 6 small
"LLAAALALLL"
=> false

@gen 7 small
"LLLALAALLA"
=> false

@gen 8 small
"LPL"
=> true

# Full size, 1000 days: a second absence on the last day, three late days
# only at the very end, and a log that passes.
@gen 2
""
=> false

@gen 10
""
=> false

@gen 14
""
=> true
